title: SINEs and Satellite DNA
eyebrow: Lesson 6 · short repeats, from one copy to a whole genome
intro: Lesson 3 masked repeats so that they would not get in the way of genes. This lesson makes two kinds of repeat the subject. SINEs are short elements that copy themselves through RNA and sit alone, between unique stretches of DNA, in hundreds of thousands of places; satellites are units repeated head to tail in long arrays. We follow a SINE through its life cycle, find every copy of a known family, discover new families, split them into subfamilies with consensus sequences, and use the presence or absence of a copy at the same place in two genomes as a character for phylogenetics. Then we turn to satellites: monomers, arrays and higher-order repeats, satellites built from pieces of SINEs, and why both young SINEs and satellite arrays are where genome assemblies break.

The examples come from our lab's own work: a rodent SINE family in species A and a close relative (search, de novo discovery and orthologous loci), the shrew-mole SINE Urop, and SINEs and satellites of bats and lizards, with unpublished results marked as such. The tools are the lab's public ones (sear, SubFam, SINEderella, SINE_orth_loc, CLsat_workflow) next to standard programs. Dating of insertions, transposable elements other than SINEs and population genetics of insertion polymorphisms are left for other lessons. Hover over a dotted term to see what it means.

steps.title: What a SINE is
steps.what: Definition, head-body-tail anatomy, copy and paste through RNA, target site duplications, subfamilies, why insertions are good markers.

steps.title: Finding copies of a known SINE
steps.what: Why seed-based tools miss old copies; Smith-Waterman in genome windows with sear; the identity and length rules; counting loci.

steps.title: Discovering new SINEs
steps.what: Signals a SINE leaves, three ways to collect candidates, the minus bank, the head test against a shuffle null, ends set by unique flanks.

steps.title: Families, subfamilies and consensus sequences
steps.what: Diagnostic positions versus private decay, consensus rules, chunk consensuses, peeling, assignment by repeated votes.

steps.title: Orthologous loci: presence and absence
steps.what: Insertions as phylogenetic characters, lineage sorting and homoplasy, matching loci by their flanks, PM/MP/SINE calls.

steps.title: Satellite DNA
steps.what: Monomers, arrays and higher-order repeats, the library hypothesis, satellites built from SINEs, dot plots, rotating to a common frame.

steps.title: Satellites and young SINEs in assemblies
steps.what: Why assemblies stop in young SINEs and collapse arrays; measuring arrays from depth and k-mers; checking the assembly with reads.

steps.title: A complete SINE study, step by step
steps.what: The lab's order of work from known SINEs to orthologous loci, with inputs, outputs and what a finished study delivers.
